There is no throttling, lockout, or rate-limiting on failed authentication attempts across any of the 6 JSON API endpoints (whoami, employees_list, employee_detail, my_compensation, documents_list, policies_list). A grep for throttle/ratelimit in the entire codebase returned zero results. While API keys have high entropy (prefix + 32 bytes base64), the absence of rate limiting enables unbounded guesses per second, weakening defense-in-depth.

extra.message: Webhook Endpoints Do Not Enforce Creator Ownership (IDOR)

metadata.proof: Any authenticated hr_admin can supply another admin's webhook_id to /api/webhooks/<id>/ (webhook_edit view). The view at line 324 loads WebhookEndpoint by primary key without filtering on created_by, so one admin can modify, delete, or otherwise interfere with another admin's endpoint. This violates object-level authorization.

extra.message: Disabling a User Does Not Invalidate Existing Sessions

metadata.proof: An hr_admin toggles another user's active flag via POST /accounts/admin/users/<id>/toggle/ at line 385. Only the database flag changes; no Django session rows for that user are flushed. The disabled user keeps full access until their session cookie expires (up to SESSION_COOKIE_AGE). The same gap exists when disabling through AdminUserForm in admin_user_edit.

extra.message: Password Change Does Not Revoke Other Active Sessions

metadata.proof: When a user changes their password via POST /accounts/password/change/ at line 172, update_session_auth_hash only refreshes the current session's hash. Any other sessions (for example, an attacker who obtained the old password via a stolen session cookie) remain valid for the remainder of the session lifetime.

extra.message: API Keys Have No Expiration — Perpetual Until Manual Revocation

metadata.proof: The APIKey model (line 20-72) has created_at, last_used_at, and revoked_at fields but no expires_at field. Once generated via APIKey.generate(), an API key remains valid indefinitely — it will never auto-expire. The only way to invalidate a key is manual revocation via api_key_revoke(). authenticate_api_key() in portal_api/services.py only checks revoked_at__isnull=True with no expiry check. If a key is leaked (logs, clipboard, compromised client), the attacker retains perpetual API access.
